title: Higher Bonferroni Inequalities for a General Finite Set Family
description: Answers the third open question of inclusion-exclusion-oq-04 (The Sieve/Dual Form of Inclusion–Exclusion): state and prove the higher Bonferroni inequalities at full generality. For an arbitrary finite family A : ι → Finset α of finite sets over a finite universe, the inclusion–exclusion sieve sum Σ_k (-1)^k S_k (with S_k = Σ_{|J|=k} |⋂_{i∈J} A i| and S_0 = |α|) equals the number of elements in none of the sets. The Bonferroni inequalities state that truncating this alternating sum at level m gives a one-sided bound on that count whose direction is the parity of m: noneCard A ≤ bonf A m when m is even, and bonf A m ≤ noneCard A when m is odd; equivalently (-1)^m (bonf A m − noneCard A) ≥ 0 for every m. The proof is a purely combinatorial per-element reindexing: writing deg A x for the number of sets containing x, a size-k index set J contributes x to S_k exactly when J ⊆ {i : x ∈ A i}, so S_k = Σ_x C(deg A x, k); exchanging the order of summation (Finset.sum_comm) gives bonf A m = Σ_x altPartial (deg A x) m, where altPartial f m = Σ_{j=0}^m (-1)^j C(f,j) is the partial alternating binomial sum. Pascal's rule telescopes altPartial 0 m = 1 and altPartial (f+1) m = (-1)^m C(f,m); elements in no set (deg = 0) reproduce noneCard exactly, and each element in ≥1 set contributes the single signed term (-1)^m C(deg−1, m) of magnitude ≥ 0. Once m ≥ |ι| the truncation is the full sieve and the two sides coincide (the exact inclusion–exclusion principle, recovered as bonf_eq_noneCard_of_card_le). This is the general theorem of which the gallery's derangement-specific Bonferroni file (inclusion-exclusion-oq-04-oq-01-oq-02) is the instance A i = {σ : σ i = i}. Self-contained, 0 axioms, 0 sorries, no native_decide.

originalContributions: bonferroni_even / bonferroni_odd: the higher Bonferroni inequalities for an arbitrary finite set family — truncating the inclusion–exclusion sieve after an even (resp. odd) layer over-counts (resp. under-counts) the number of elements lying in none of the sets. This general one-sided bracketing of #(none) is not in Mathlib (which has only the exact inclusion–exclusion identity) nor previously in the gallery at this generality (only the derangement instance).

bonf_eq_sum_altPartial: the per-element reindexing bonf A m = Σ_x altPartial (deg A x) m, obtained by writing each sieve layer as a filter cardinality, exchanging the (subset, element) double sum (Finset.sum_comm), and collapsing the size-k index sets containing a fixed element to C(deg A x, k). This is the engine that turns a sum over 2^|ι| subsets into a sum over elements weighted by their partial alternating binomial sums.

altPartial_succ: Pascal telescoping of the partial alternating binomial sum, Σ_{j=0}^m (-1)^j C(f+1,j) = (-1)^m C(f,m), proved by induction on m. The collapse to a single signed term is what pins the sign of the truncation error to (-1)^m.

neg_one_pow_mul_bonf_sub_nonneg: the unified signed statement (-1)^m (bonf A m − noneCard A) ≥ 0 for every truncation level m, from which both parity inequalities follow by specializing the sign of (-1)^m. Each element contributes either 0 (in no set) or the non-negative C(deg−1, m) (in ≥1 set).

bonf_eq_noneCard_of_card_le: the exact inclusion–exclusion principle recovered as the m ≥ |ι| endpoint of the Bonferroni ladder — once the truncation reaches the number of indices the partial alternating sum becomes the exact indicator of 'in no set', so the truncated sieve equals the true count.

Modeling 'higher Bonferroni' over an abstract family A : ι → Finset α with deg A x = #{i : x ∈ A i}: the element-degree formulation that makes the entire proof a pointwise statement about partial alternating binomial sums, with the derangement sieve (inclusion-exclusion-oq-04-oq-01-oq-02) the special case A i = {σ : σ i = i}.

overview.historicalContext: The Bonferroni inequalities, introduced by Carlo Emilio Bonferroni in 1936, refine the inclusion–exclusion principle into a ladder of one-sided estimates: stopping the alternating sieve sum early yields an upper or a lower bound on the quantity being counted, with the direction governed by where the truncation falls. They are a workhorse of probability (the Bonferroni correction for simultaneous statistical inference is the most familiar incarnation) and of analytic and probabilistic combinatorics, where the truncated sieve gives quantitative control when the full inclusion–exclusion sum is intractable. The classical statement bounds P(∪ A_i) or the count of elements in at least one set; the dual form bounds the count of elements in none. This entry formalizes the dual higher Bonferroni inequalities for an arbitrary finite family of sets — the general theorem behind the gallery's derangement-specific instance — recovering the exact inclusion–exclusion principle as the endpoint of the bracketing ladder.
overview.problemStatement: Let A : ι → Finset α be a finite family of finite sets over a finite universe, and let S_k = Σ_{|J|=k} |⋂_{i∈J} A i| be the k-th sieve layer (S_0 = |α|). Define the truncated sieve bonf A m = Σ_{k=0}^m (-1)^k S_k and let noneCard A be the number of elements lying in none of the A i. Prove the higher Bonferroni inequalities: noneCard A ≤ bonf A m when m is even, bonf A m ≤ noneCard A when m is odd — equivalently (-1)^m (bonf A m − noneCard A) ≥ 0 for every m — and show that for m ≥ |ι| the truncation is exact (bonf A m = noneCard A).
overview.proofStrategy: Reduce the whole statement to a pointwise fact about partial alternating binomial sums. For x : α let deg A x = #{i : x ∈ A i}. Each size-k index set J contributes x to S_k exactly when J ⊆ {i : x ∈ A i}, so writing every layer as a filter cardinality, exchanging the (subset J, element x) double sum (Finset.sum_comm), and collapsing the contained size-k index sets to C(deg A x, k) (filter_forall_eq_powersetCard + Finset.card_powersetCard) gives bonf A m = Σ_x altPartial (deg A x) m, where altPartial f m = Σ_{j=0}^m (-1)^j C(f,j). Pascal's rule telescopes altPartial 0 m = 1 and altPartial (f+1) m = (-1)^m C(f,m) (altPartial_succ). Subtracting the indicator form of noneCard, the per-element truncation error is 0 for elements in no set and (-1)^m C(deg−1, m) for elements in ≥1 set, so (-1)^m times it is non-negative term-by-term (neg_one_pow_mul_term_nonneg); summing gives the core sign statement, and specializing the parity of m yields the two inequalities. For m ≥ |ι|, deg A x ≤ |ι| ≤ m forces C(deg−1, m) = 0, collapsing altPartial to the exact indicator and recovering bonf A m = noneCard A.
keyInsights: The general higher Bonferroni inequalities are a pointwise statement in disguise: every element contributes its own partial alternating binomial sum altPartial (deg A x) m, and the sign of the whole truncation error is forced term-by-term by the sign of these contributions. No global cancellation argument is needed — the bracketing is visible element by element.

Exchanging the order of summation is the entire combinatorial content. Once Finset.sum_comm moves the element sum outside the (size k, subset J) sums, the family A disappears and only deg A x survives; the sieve over 2^|ι| subsets becomes a sum over |α| elements weighted by binomial coefficients.

Pascal telescoping pins the sign. The partial alternating binomial sum collapses to the single signed term (-1)^m C(f,m), so the magnitude C(deg−1, m) ≥ 0 is non-negative and the sign is exactly (-1)^m — the parity of the truncation level, which is the Bonferroni phenomenon.

The exact inclusion–exclusion principle is just the endpoint of the Bonferroni ladder. Truncating at m ≥ |ι| kills every binomial coefficient C(deg−1, m) by Nat.choose_eq_zero_of_lt, so the partial alternating sum becomes the exact indicator of 'in no set' and the truncated sieve equals the true count — the inequalities and the identity are one continuous family.

Signs must live in ℤ. The alternating sieve cannot be phrased over ℕ (truncated subtraction would corrupt it), so bonf, the layers, and altPartial are all integer-valued; the inequalities are integer inequalities, exactly the subtlety the dual sieve is designed to expose.

The derangement Bonferroni file is literally this theorem at A i = {σ : σ i = i}. The per-permutation reindexing of the gallery's InclusionExclusionSieveDerangementsBonferroni is the special case of the per-element reindexing here, confirming that the general statement is the right level of abstraction.

sections.title: The Partial Alternating Binomial Sum
sections.summary: altPartial f m is the alternating binomial sum truncated at m. altPartial_zero shows it is 1 when f = 0, and altPartial_succ telescopes it by Pascal's rule to the single signed term (-1)^m C(f,m); altPartial_of_le notes that for m ≥ f it becomes the exact indicator of f = 0. These are the only number-theoretic inputs to the whole argument.

sections.title: The Family, Its Degrees, and the Truncated Sieve
sections.mathContext: $\deg_A x = \#\{i : x \in A_i\}, \quad S_k = \sum_{|J|=k} |\textstyle\bigcap_{i\in J} A_i|, \quad \mathrm{bonf}(A,m) = \sum_{k=0}^m (-1)^k S_k$
sections.summary: deg A x counts the sets containing x; sieveLayer A k is the k-th sieve layer S_k (the intersection over J recorded as the elements lying in A i for every i ∈ J, with J = ∅ giving all of α); bonf A m is the sieve sum truncated after the size-m layer; noneCard A is the number of elements in none of the sets.

sections.title: The Per-Element Reindexing
sections.summary: filter_forall_eq_powersetCard identifies the size-k index sets all of whose members contain x with the size-k subsets of {i : x ∈ A i}. bonf_eq_sum_altPartial then writes each layer as an indicator sum (Finset.card_filter), exchanges the order of summation (Finset.sum_comm), and collapses the contained index sets to C(deg A x, k) — yielding bonf A m = Σ_x altPartial (deg A x) m.

sections.title: The Bonferroni Inequalities
sections.summary: noneCard_eq_indicator_sum writes noneCard as Σ_x [deg A x = 0]. bonf_sub_noneCard expresses the truncation error as a single sum over the universe; neg_one_pow_mul_term_nonneg shows each term times (-1)^m is non-negative (0 for elements in no set, C(deg−1,m) otherwise), giving the core sign statement neg_one_pow_mul_bonf_sub_nonneg, from which bonferroni_even and bonferroni_odd follow by the parity of (-1)^m.

sections.title: Consistency with the Exact Sieve
sections.summary: deg_le_card bounds every element degree by |ι|. bonf_eq_noneCard_of_card_le then shows that once the truncation reaches the number of indices, each altPartial (deg A x) m equals the exact indicator [deg A x = 0], so the truncated sieve equals the true count — the exact inclusion–exclusion principle as the endpoint of the Bonferroni ladder.

conclusion.summary: The higher Bonferroni inequalities are proved for an arbitrary finite family of finite sets: truncating the inclusion–exclusion sieve after an even layer over-counts, and after an odd layer under-counts, the number of elements in none of the sets, with the unified bound (-1)^m (bonf A m − noneCard A) ≥ 0 for every m. The argument reduces everything to a pointwise fact — each element contributes the partial alternating binomial sum of the number of sets containing it, which Pascal's rule collapses to a single signed term — so the bracketing is visible element by element. Truncating at m ≥ |ι| recovers the exact inclusion–exclusion principle. Self-contained, 0 axioms, 0 sorries, no native_decide.
conclusion.implications: This is the general theorem behind the gallery's derangement-specific Bonferroni file: that entry is the instance A i = {σ : σ i = i} over the permutation universe, and its per-permutation reindexing is the special case of the per-element reindexing here. The result adds the dual Bonferroni bracketing for arbitrary set families to the gallery (Mathlib has only the exact inclusion–exclusion identity), and packages the exact principle as the endpoint of a continuous ladder of one-sided estimates.
openQuestions: Derive the at-least-one-set (primal) Bonferroni inequalities |∪ A_i| bracketed by the truncated sieve Σ_{k=1}^m (-1)^{k-1} S_k, by complementation from the dual form proved here, and identify the exact relation between the two truncation parities.

Quantify the Bonferroni gap: bound bonf A m − noneCard A by the next layer term S_{m+1}, sharpening the one-sided inequality to the standard 'error is at most the first omitted term' Bonferroni estimate.
